refinement.title: Cyan · open a clear view.
refinement.problem: The piece was released, but a finger still covered the bead needed by the next visual check.
refinement.result: The wider opening exposed Cyan, earned two accepted observations, and enabled the continuous run to place all twelve pieces.

attempts.label: Release
attempts.attempt: The original opening left the next RGB check unaccepted.
attempts.diagnosis: The moving finger still crossed the middle bead in the top image.
attempts.change: Use the recorded joint state and public finger mesh to locate the occlusion.
attempts.outcome: The geometry identified the finger responsible.

attempts.label: Calculate
attempts.diagnosis: A small increase still left some bead rays blocked.
attempts.change: Select the smallest tested opening that cleared every sampled ray and passed the existing guards.
attempts.outcome: The calculation selected a 75 mm opening.

attempts.label: Replay
attempts.attempt: Execute the revised opening and look again.
attempts.outcome: Cyan passed release and next-piece handoff checks; independent audit confirmed all twelve physical placements at the end of the run.

refinement.caption: A wider opening reveals the bead and lets the policy continue.

refinement.title: Red · seat the receiving grasp.
refinement.problem: A jaw could look loaded while holding the edge of a bead, allowing the piece to roll.
refinement.result: In the continuous twelve-piece run, Red passed both handoffs and its final release. Independent audit confirmed the completed physical assembly.

evidence.label: See the refinement record
evidence.scope: Recorded attempts, local changes, and verification.

attempts.label: Diagnose
attempts.attempt: Earlier handoffs passed, but the held piece rolled during the follow-up motion.
attempts.diagnosis: RGB and robot kinematics placed the bead beyond the front of the blade.
attempts.change: Check the actual finite contact face throughout closing.
attempts.outcome: Saved observations explained why a loaded jaw alone was insufficient.

attempts.label: Repair
attempts.attempt: Keep the donor holding while the receiver is corrected.
attempts.diagnosis: Closing can move the far bead away from its preclose position.
attempts.change: Reopen locally, reobserve, recenter, and reclose under the same geometry checks.
attempts.outcome: The bounded recovery and contact checks passed independent API review.

attempts.label: Rejoin
attempts.attempt: Run both handoffs with fresh receiver bindings in the complete sequence.
attempts.outcome: All eight Red transfer windows and its release passed. The final physical assembly and arms-home state passed independent audit.

refinement.caption: Recenter while supported, regrasp, and finish the placement.

generalization.title: Move the source or the board.
generalization.claim: The same frozen Azure module completed three selected physical rehearsals.
generalization.observed: Nominal; source shifted 3 mm and rotated 3°; board shifted 2 mm and rotated 0.5°. All three released stably, with 0.45–0.75 mm final bead error. The observed source changed the grasp target; the observed board changed the transport target.
generalization.scope: One-piece control · three selected scene variations.

evidence.label: Physical variation results
evidence.scope: Azure only; these are not complete-assembly robustness trials.

generalization.title: Change the input, change the plan.
generalization.claim: The current Cyan and Red functions generate targets from measured poses and robot state.
generalization.observed: A [3, −2, 1] mm board shift moves Cyan's target by the same amount. A 4° source rotation changes Red's first grasp-check orientation by 4°. Increasing board uncertainty can turn an admitted clearance into a refusal. All 16 offline input-response checks passed.
generalization.scope: Offline checks of the actual policy functions.

evidence.label: Inputs and generated outputs
evidence.scope: Demonstrates input-dependent planning and refusal, not physical success under these perturbations.

generalization.title: Recognize shape across appearance.
generalization.claim: Piece identity can be recovered when the colors are shuffled or removed.
generalization.observed: Across three development scenes per appearance, the shape estimator recovered 36/36 pieces with shuffled colors and 36/36 with all-gray pieces. Maximum bead error was 0.75 mm and 0.90 mm respectively.
generalization.scope: Shape perception · three scenes per appearance.

intro.title: From a real puzzle to a visual robot policy.
intro.description: Twelve pieces, two arms. Reconstruct the scene, compose a feedback-driven policy, and improve it through physical trials.
intro.policyInputs: RGB images, robot joint state, and known geometry.
intro.policyBehavior: The graph chooses the next skill; each skill generates targets from the current observations. Independent physical checks evaluate the execution.

methodAlignment.title: RSS scene → typed skills → parallel trials → refine → verify.
methodAlignment.description: GaP decomposes the task into reusable skills with typed inputs and independent checkpoints. Failed rehearsals identify the module to repair; the revised skills are then tested together.

steps.title: Reconstruct with RSS
steps.description: Build the scene, task specification, robot embodiment, and contact simulation from the real demonstration.

steps.title: Author with GaP
steps.description: Use the supported graph builder, typed skill contracts, conditional exits, and checkpoint sidecars, guided by the upstream skill and authoring prompts.

steps.title: Control from observation
steps.description: Generate actions from RGB estimates, measured robot joints, public forward kinematics, and known geometry.

steps.title: Rehearse and repair
steps.description: Explore modules and short sequences in parallel, diagnose the failed condition, refine the responsible skill, and reconnect the graph.

steps.title: Evaluate independently
steps.description: Independent physical checkpoints check the actual grasp, handover, placement, stability, and final robot state.
